profile.summary: MPNN, the message passing neural network, is a general family of graph neural networks rather than a single trained model. A molecule or other graph is read as nodes and edges; the model learns a message passing algorithm and an aggregation procedure that compute a function of the whole graph, which is mapped to the property being predicted. The name appears on this benchmark database because the DeepProtein benchmark trained an MPNN as a baseline on protein tasks.

summary_quotes.text: we reformulate existing models into a single common framework we call Message Passing Neural Networks (MPNNs) and explore additional novel variations within this framework
These models learn a message passing algorithm and aggregation procedure to compute a function of their entire input graph.
MPNN is a GNN variant that considers passing messages (and modeling interactions) between both edges and nodes based on their neighbors.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: In the paper's framework, the model learns a message passing algorithm and an aggregation procedure that compute a function of the whole input graph. Unlike the simpler graph convolution and graph attention baselines, an MPNN uses edge features as well as node features. In the DeepProtein configuration the readout is Sum and Max and the node and edge embedding dimension is 64, with the number of message passing steps set by the encoder's num_timesteps argument.

sections.title: What has been released
sections.body: An open source implementation of the paper is at github.com/brain-research/mpnn under the Apache 2.0 licence. Its README states that it contains only the model class definition and some unit tests, that a dataset reader and basic trainer were planned for a future release, and that it is not an official Google product. It also notes that the default hyperparameters give reasonable performance on all targets but that the numbers in the paper came from a separate hyperparameter search with 50 trials per target. There are no trained weights.

sections.title: Use as a benchmark baseline
sections.body: The DeepProtein benchmark did not use the brain-research/mpnn reference code. Its encoder imports MPNNGNN from the dgllife library and adds a Sum and Max readout and a linear layer to the predictor dimension. A protein result reported against the name MPNN is therefore a dgllife message passing network that the benchmark trained on that task. The DeepProtein README states that its legacy graph encoders, DGL_MPNN among them, are not available in its version 2 runtime.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: A framework of graph neural networks for supervised learning on graphs, trained per task. Not a pretrained model.

quotes.text: we reformulate existing models into a single common framework we call Message Passing Neural Networks (MPNNs)

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Message passing between neighbouring nodes with edge features, followed by an aggregation and a graph-level readout. In the DeepProtein configuration: Sum and Max readout, node and edge embedding dimension 64.
facts.source_locator: arXiv abstract; DeepProtein full text, MPNN paragraph

quotes.text: These models learn a message passing algorithm and aggregation procedure to compute a function of their entire input graph.

MPNN is a GNN variant that considers passing messages (and modeling interactions) between both edges and nodes based on their neighbors. Edge features are included necessarily compared with GCN and GAT. Readout function is Sum And Max. Node and edge embedding dimension is 64.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: A graph with node and edge features. Edge features are required, unlike the graph convolution and graph attention baselines. In the protein benchmark the graph is built from the sequence by way of a SMILES string, with edge features added by an edge featuriser.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: A graph-level prediction for the trained task, for example a molecular property. In the benchmark encoder the pooled features go through a linear layer to the predictor dimension.

notes: MPNN is an architecture family, not a released model. The record exists because DeepProtein trained an MPNN baseline on protein tasks, using dgllife's MPNNGNN. The open source implementation brain-research/mpnn holds the model class and unit tests under Apache 2.0 and carries the disclaimer that it is not an official Google product, so calling it the official release is a judgement a reviewer may want to revisit. Only the arXiv abstract page was read; the paper PDF was not fetched. A reviewer may prefer to mark this record as a baseline architecture rather than a model with a release.
